The helper preserves UTF-8 prompt payload, replaces the command argument with stdin marker and returns that payload separately; this is transport behavior, not provider-served model attestation.

The timeout writer constructs complete bytes, writes/fsyncs a private same-directory staging inode, and atomically links without replacing the destination. Interrupted staging is not a final report; no blocked-filesystem or power-loss guarantee follows.

Once timeout is decided, the sole evidence attempt precedes deadline-consuming cleanup. Existing hard alarm, worker/deadline calculations, cancellation and timeout exit remain separate; elapsed_ms samples payload construction, not completed cleanup.

Three regression methods run six real-supervisor barrier scenarios for cleanup ordering, empty/prefix interruption, completed publication and raced file/symlink refusal. Each requires reached barriers, actual timeout and owned-worker cleanup; original eight methods remain separate.
Applicable producer stages expose the ShipLoop planning guide and record-only check; the comment records that no standalone child or backchain_passes option remains.
The complete retained dependency audit is ShipLoop planning guidance; it does not invoke the retired standalone skill.
The exact graph schema and invariants consumed by the record-only check now live in the ShipLoop guide.
Record-only backchain-check reads candidate graph bytes, validates them, and records a receipt without changing run state; this does not prove a live host read its locator.
Saved state containing backchain_passes is rejected with BACKCHAIN_PASSES_REASON before normal state-key validation; no migration occurs.
The refusal identifies the retired run option and gives the fresh-run hint rather than silently migrating the saved run.
